content.jointProblem: What combination of weld condition, cyclic loading, temperature history and moisture exposure explains cracking in AutomVoj’s painted mild-steel conveyor joints, and which manufacturing or design changes could reduce it? The first experiment should compare representative production joints under measured service loading at room temperature and at 2–6 °C, with controlled condensation where feasible, to test whether Erić’s thermo-mechanical fatigue methods transfer to this application.

rationale.text: Erić has experimentally investigated the interaction of mechanical fatigue and thermal cycling in welded structural steel, directly relevant to testing AutomVoj’s suspected combined-loading mechanism.

sources.quote: Four loading programmes were applied: isothermal fatigue at 20 °C, isothermal fatigue at −30 °C, in-phase thermo-mechanical fatigue (TMF), and out-of-phase TMF, with twelve specimens per programme.

rationale.text: His field-assessment experience provides a basis for constructing tests from operational load and temperature histories rather than relying only on workshop loading.

sources.quote: Rainflow-counted stress spectra and simultaneous temperature records were used to construct a combined loading environment for assessment.

rationale.text: He has combined residual-stress measurements with finite-element modelling of welded joints, relevant to investigating whether weld-induced stresses contribute to the failures.

sources.quote: Residual stress relaxation in S355 cruciform fillet-welded joints was tracked over 10, 100, 1000, and 10 000 fatigue cycles
A cyclic plasticity FE model employing a Chaboche kinematic hardening rule reproduced the surface relaxation trend within 12% across all conditions.

rationale.text: His group routinely uses fatigue-testing, climate-control and simulation resources relevant to addressing the company’s current testing gap.

sources.quote: The group routinely uses servo-hydraulic fatigue testing machines, a climate chamber capable of reaching −60 °C, and in-house FE models

rationale.text: A joint project is consistent with his stated interest in company collaboration on low-temperature and combined-loading fatigue testing.

sources.quote: joint projects involving fatigue testing under low-temperature or combined loading conditions

constraints.text: The experimental baseline must represent the actual chilled service environment and distinguish measured conditions from the company’s unverified thermal-cycling, condensation and vibration hypothesis.

sources.quote: Our suspicion is that the combination of thermal cycling, condensation, and the vibration load from loaded belts is doing something

constraints.text: Failure analysis and test specimens must represent the painted mild-steel hollow-section construction and the crossmember-to-stringer detail; access to the retained failed sections and site records must be arranged.

sources.quote: Our conveyor frames are welded from mild steel hollow section and painted for corrosion resistance before delivery.
weld joint cracking at the main crossmember-to-stringer connections
We have photos and measurements of the cracked joints from site visits, and we still have two of the failed sections in storage.

constraints.text: The test plan must address the approximately 18-month service failure rather than treating passage of a room-temperature load test as evidence of durability.

sources.quote: after about 18 months of continuous use.
We test frames under load at room temperature and they pass without any problem.

constraints.text: Combined environmental fatigue testing requires external facilities and advance equipment booking; chamber, fixture and humidity-control suitability must be confirmed before committing to a campaign.

sources.quote: We do not currently have the equipment or know-how to test at low temperatures under cyclic load.
Erić's climate chamber and servo-hydraulic machine are shared with two other research groups; scheduling access for extended test campaigns requires advance coordination.

constraints.text: Company engineering effort must be explicitly allocated around live-project commitments because there is no dedicated R&D team.

sources.quote: We have no dedicated R&D department
our chief engineer and two senior automation engineers who allocate time between live projects and improvement work.

risks: The strongest thermal-fatigue evidence concerns other steel grades, joint geometries and substantially colder conditions. Its relevance to painted mild-steel hollow sections at 2–6 °C is unvalidated and must be tested in the first comparative experiment.

Condensation-assisted damage and coating effects are not demonstrated in the supplied researcher evidence. Additional corrosion expertise or environmental-test capability may be needed if initial failure analysis implicates them.
The company’s proposed mechanism may be incomplete or incorrect; fabrication defects, local stress concentration or unmeasured operating loads could dominate.
Accelerating an approximately 18-month failure could change the damage mechanism, so short laboratory tests may not establish service-life improvement.
Researcher availability is unknown, and shared equipment could delay testing. Company staff also divide improvement work with live projects.
Budget, delivery deadline, customer-site access and the availability of production and operational records are unknown; these could limit failure reproduction and validation.
questions: What is Erić’s availability, and when can the shared fatigue machine and climate chamber be reserved?
Can the laboratory accommodate the required joint dimensions and loads while controlling and measuring temperature, humidity and condensation at 2–6 °C?
Can AutomVoj provide the two failed sections, unfailed comparison joints, drawings, steel and filler specifications, welding procedures, inspection records and coating details?
Can customer sites be instrumented to record joint strains, vibration, belt loading, start-stop events, temperature and humidity, including cleaning or defrost cycles?
What do the fracture surfaces and crack locations indicate, and is specialist corrosion analysis needed before defining the fatigue programme?
What budget, deadline and company engineering time are available, and who will approve and manufacture trial changes?
What evidence will be required to accept a proposed change, including replication, preservation of the field failure mechanism and follow-up in service?
